_comment: One-way ceiling on oversized source files, per package. The number is Σ max(0, lines − 500) — the total lines past the limit, NOT a file count, so splitting a large file always lowers it and never trips the gate. check-file-size-ratchet.ts fails when a package's number RISES. After splitting something, run `pnpm lint:file-size --update` to lock the win; --update never raises a floor. Raising a number requires editing this file in the same PR.
_apps_api_src_note: 44022 → 44026 (+4) for the null-handling that extractJsonFromLlm's honest contract forces on its callers. The util used to fabricate `{ [fallbackKey]: response } as T` on total parse failure; removing that makes the return `T | null`, and eight files now say `?? {}` or widen a type to optional. All four lines land in files already past 500. Splitting a service so a `?? {}` fits is the ratchet driving the design; the file actually worth splitting here is application-analysis-workflow.service.ts at 3856 lines, and doing that takes this number back down.
_apps_api_prisma_note: 11948 → 11953 (+5) for the Penn testing-policy row. The 2026-07-24 audit held Penn at UNKNOWN pending an August recheck; the recheck landed and the row plus its evidence note is what grew the seed. The alternative to raising this is splitting seed-testing-policy-2026-07-25.ts, which would put a five-line data row behind a file split — the ratchet driving the design rather than the other way round. The oversized file here is seed-all-features.ts (3458 lines); that is the one worth splitting, and doing so takes this number back down.
